parsedVerdict.reasoning: AdvanceOrderUseCase is a typical application-layer use case. It loads the aggregate through a repository port, hands the state transition to the domain (order.advanceTo), calls a domain service (StockReservationService.dispatch) when a step completes, saves the result through the port and maps it to a DTO. The file contains no persistence, transport or framework code: all I/O goes through injected domain ports. The `if (target === 'shipped')` branch is the one borderline point. It triggers dispatching across collaborators after a transition rather than deciding whether the transition is allowed, so it reads as application-level coordination of a domain service, not misplaced business logic. Still, one could argue it encodes a domain policy that would fit better in the aggregate or a domain event handler. ExecuteContextDto is a plain application-layer input DTO. No ADR prose is given that contradicts this.
